title: 2006 AMC 8 Problem 5
statement: Points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D\) are midpoints of the sides of the larger square. If the larger square has area \(60,\) what is the area of the smaller square?

solutions.text:
Note that we can fold all the triangles in to perfectly cover the smaller square. This means that area of the smaller square is half the area of the larger square.

This makes the area of the smaller square \(60 \div 2 = 30.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The four corner triangles around the smaller square are congruent.
Those four outside triangles can be rearranged to cover the smaller square.
